title: Codex Telegram Supervision Workspace
purpose: Define the authority, identity, recovery, isolation, review, browser, recipe, and release contracts for supervising Codex work across private self-hosted workers.
scope: This specification covers the staged supervision workspace roadmap. It establishes the durable Telegram update receipt and bounded Task/Run/Command, delivery, approval/input, claim, recovery-action, restart-reconciliation, review-packet, Telegram-handoff, task-workspace allocation, explicit Telegram task-flow, opt-in browser-pairing projection, local worker-boundary, authenticated coordinator registration, coordinator lease-handoff, recipe, and staged update slices.

authority.telegram: authentication, operator control, and consequential approval
authority.codex: thread and turn execution plus execution provenance
authority.local_persistence: supervision metadata, command receipts, acknowledgements, claims, leases, and recovery evidence; never a replacement for Codex history

requirements.title: Preserve authority boundaries
requirements.statement: The host MUST keep Telegram as the authentication, operator-control, and consequential-approval authority; Codex MUST remain the execution and execution-provenance authority; and the Mini App and browser surfaces MUST remain read-only until a separately approved authorization contract exists.

requirements.title: Separate application identity from Codex provenance
requirements.statement: The durable supervision model MUST distinguish ConversationId, TaskId, RunId, CommandId, ApprovalId, WorkerId, WorkspaceId, LeaseId, and RecipeVersion from Codex thread and turn identifiers; Codex identifiers MUST be retained as provenance and MUST NOT be treated as substitutes for application identity.

requirements.title: Record Telegram update delivery idempotency
requirements.statement: The Telegram update boundary MUST atomically persist a bounded receipt for each positive Telegram update ID, reject completed or non-expired in-flight replays, reclaim expired in-flight receipts, and remain backward compatible with state files that predate the receipt collection.
notes: Telegram UpdateId is a transport receipt key, not the future application-owned CommandId.
A handler failure abandons the receipt for retry; an unclean process termination leaves a lease that can be reclaimed after expiry.

requirements.title: Separate execution and delivery lifecycle
requirements.statement: Durable supervision records MUST represent execution lifecycle, approval state, claim or recovery state, and Telegram delivery state as separate dimensions so a failed notification cannot turn a completed Codex run into a failed run and an ambiguous execution cannot be blindly replayed.

requirements.title: Fail closed on unsafe scope or approval
requirements.statement: Unknown, malformed, stale, replayed, cross-user, cross-chat, cross-topic, or ambiguous control and approval actions MUST fail closed; recovery MUST preserve evidence and MUST NOT blindly resend a side-effecting Codex command.

requirements.title: Keep later worker and review contracts inspectable
requirements.statement: Review packets, task workspaces, worker routing, browser pairing, recipes, and worker updates MUST carry bounded provenance, explicit ownership, compatibility and lifecycle state, and operator-visible evidence before they are exposed as a user-visible capability.

requirements.title: Keep worker leases bounded and drain-aware
requirements.statement: A local worker MUST have a stable persisted WorkerId, bounded concurrent task leases, Codex-backed readiness, and an explicit draining state; lease acquisition MUST be serialized and idempotent by TaskId, reclaim expired leases before capacity checks, reject new leases while draining, and MUST NOT interrupt an existing Codex session when draining begins.

requirements.title: Snapshot task recipes by version
requirements.statement: A task recipe MUST expose a stable RecipeId and RecipeVersion plus bounded objective, session policy, expected outputs, and required capabilities; selecting a recipe MUST snapshot its identity into the task provenance and MUST NOT rewrite an existing task when configuration changes.

requirements.title: Authenticate and bound coordinator worker registration
requirements.statement: An optional coordinator MUST accept only exact bearer-token worker heartbeats, optionally bind admission to configured WorkerIds, cap persisted remote workers, retain only bounded worker status metadata, and project missed heartbeats as unavailable; the coordinator MUST NOT receive Codex credentials or become the local worker's execution authority.

requirements.title: Stage worker updates without replacing the protected installation
requirements.statement: An enabled worker update MUST require an explicitly configured package path, target release version, SHA-256 digest, and operator-owned staging root; staging MUST require the local worker to be drained with zero active leases, verify the package digest, version, and required capabilities, persist bounded outcome evidence, and capture a last-known-good executable for explicit rollback; the application MUST NOT overwrite its protected running installation or claim post-install health before an external installer verifies it.

requirements.title: Use authenticated, idempotent coordinator lease handoff
requirements.statement: A coordinator lease handoff MUST select only a fresh, ready, capacity-available worker with the requested capabilities and a configured private control endpoint, persist the bounded grant before sending it, expire the grant within five minutes, and return the existing active grant for repeated TaskId requests; the worker MUST authenticate the grant, bind it to its own WorkerId, re-check local readiness, draining, capabilities, and capacity, and acquire the lease through its local worker registry.

requirements.title: Record authenticated worker update completion evidence
requirements.statement: A staged worker update MUST become active only after an authenticated external installer reports the running release version, SHA-256, and health result; the manager MUST compare the report with the staged target or rollback artifact and local ready state, record a bounded health-verification or health-failure outcome, and MUST NOT claim activation from staging alone.

non_goals: A competing task database or replacement for Codex history
Browser prompts, approvals, steering, retries, cancellation, file writes, uploads, commits, merges, or deployments
Blind replay of side-effecting work after a crash or timeout
Autonomous merge, push, deploy, or release
Public multi-tenant hosting or broad implicit Telegram authorization
